Topics · One God, one message

Is my school or my grandfather right about God?

No one is excused from proof: not school, grandfather or this app. The Quran itself says 'bring your proof'.

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَمَّن يَبْدَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَمَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Is He [not best] who begins creation and then repeats it and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a deity with Allāh? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."

Quran · An-Naml 27:64

Translation

For who is God, except Yahweh? Who is a rock, besides our God,

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י מִ֣י אֱ֭לוֹהַּ מִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וּמִ֥י צ֝֗וּר זוּלָתִ֥י אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

the Psalms · 18:31

World English Bible

Neither gets a pass here: not the school, not the grandfather, not this app. The passage asks who begins creation and repeats it, who provides from heaven and earth, and then it says, bring your proof, if you are truthful. It makes proof the standard, and a standard binds everyone who uses it, including those who agree with the book.

A question for you

What would you check first?

If you sayWhat school taught me.
ThenThen ask: what was the evidence, and what would have counted as evidence? That is the very demand in the verse.
If you sayWhat my grandfather does.
ThenHe is under the same demand. The verse excuses no one.
If you sayWhat I actually experience.
ThenExperience is a real witness. The next passage gives a rule for weighing what you hear and see.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not pursue[745] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

Translator's notes

[745] i.e., do not assume and do not say.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

Original · Ancient Greek

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:36-37

World English Bible

The verse does not tell you to believe your grandfather instead of your teacher. It says: do not pursue what you have no knowledge of; hearing, sight and the heart will each be asked about. Where one generation was told what to think and the next was told the opposite, this is a rule for anyone: check what reaches your ears, your eyes and your heart before you carry it.

A question for you

How do you decide whom to trust now?

If you sayBy who tells the truth when it costs them.
ThenAn old and good test, and one that hearing and heart are asked to apply.
If you sayBy who I can check.
ThenThat is what the verse asks: do not follow what you have no knowledge of.
If you sayBy who has no reason to lie to me.
ThenA good start, and you add to it by checking what they say.

Part 3 of 3

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُۥٓ ۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمْ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones Allāh has guided, and those are people of understanding.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:18

Translation

It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!” But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας· αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

the Gospel (Luke) · 11:27-28

World English Bible

There is a third rule, and it is the kindest: those who listen to what is said and follow the best of it. Not the loudest, not the official. The best. It means you may listen to your teacher and your grandfather, and keep what is good in both, so long as you test it. It is a method for a person who has been burned by slogans: listen to all, keep what holds.

A question for you

How do you tell the best of what you hear?

If you sayIt still stands when I am tired and no one is watching.
ThenA strict test, and close to what the verse calls 'the best'.
If you sayIt treats people well.
ThenThat is a measure everyone knows, and it needs no certificate.
If you sayIt holds when I test it.
ThenThat is what the three verses ask together.

The same in the other books

Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue. In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 360-361

Max Müller, 1881

Translation

He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
